# Determining $\Re f(0)$ for a Degenerate Limit of Conformal Maps

## Setting Up the Parametrization

Every conformal bijection from $\mathbb{D}$ onto $\mathbb{A} = \{\Re z > 0\}$ can be written as:
$$f(z) = \frac{1+\phi(z)}{1-\phi(z)}$$
where $\phi \in \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$, the group of conformal automorphisms of the disk:
$$\phi(z) = e^{i\theta}\frac{z-a}{1-\bar{a}z}, \quad |a|<1,\; \theta\in\mathbb{R}.$$

## Analyzing the Limit via the Compact-Open Topology

Since $\{f_n\}$ converges uniformly on compact subsets, the corresponding automorphisms $\{\phi_n\}$ converge uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb{D}$ to some holomorphic map $\phi$. By the standard theory of the automorphism group of $\mathbb{D}$, the limit $\phi$ is either:

**Case 1: $|a| < 1$ (interior parameter).** Then $\phi$ is itself an automorphism of $\mathbb{D}$, making $f$ a conformal map from $\mathbb{D}$ to $\mathbb{A}$, hence **one-to-one**. This contradicts the hypothesis.

**Case 2: $|a| = 1$ (boundary parameter).** Then for any $z \in \mathbb{D}$:
$$\frac{z-a}{1-\bar{a}z} = \frac{a(z-a)}{a-z} = -a \quad (\text{since } \bar{a} = 1/a).$$
So $\phi_n(z) \to -e^{i\theta}a =: c$, a **constant** with $|c|=1$.

## Computing the Limit Function

In Case 2, the limit is:
$$f(z) = \frac{1+c}{1-c}, \quad |c|=1,\; c\neq 1.$$

Computing the real part:
$$\frac{1+c}{1-c} = \frac{(1+c)(1-\bar{c})}{|1-c|^2} = \frac{1-\bar{c}+c-c\bar{c}}{|1-c|^2} = \frac{c-\bar{c}}{|1-c|^2} = \frac{2i\,\Im(c)}{|1-c|^2}.$$

This is **purely imaginary**, so:
$$\Re f(0) = 0.$$

## Verifying Consistency

- Since $\Re f_n > 0$ on $\mathbb{D}$ for all $n$, uniform convergence gives $\Re f \geq 0$.  
- If $\Re f(0) = 0$ and $\Re f$ is harmonic, the minimum principle forces $\Re f \equiv 0$, so $f$ is a constant purely imaginary number — indeed **not one-to-one**. ✓

**Concrete check:** Take $a_n = 1-\tfrac{1}{n}$, $\theta_n = 0$. Then $\phi_n \to -1$, and $f_n \to \frac{1+(-1)}{1-(-1)} = 0$, giving $\Re f(0) = 0$. ✓

## Conclusion

The only way the limit $f$ fails to be one-to-one is when it degenerates to a constant on the boundary $\partial\mathbb{A} = i\mathbb{R}$, forcing:

$$\boxed{0}$$
